items.headline: The arm you have been waiting several editions for — the one that lets each motif learn its own sharpness, so you could read off whether real motifs pick a single mode or blend several — reported, and it argues against itself. Sharpness fell to a mean of 0.433, with 90% of motifs pushed toward winner-take-all and not one toward graded mixing, and the model lost 6.8 points doing it. The gradient reliably drives sharpening even though sharpening is worse, which makes this a training pathology rather than a fact about binding: you cannot quote the learned value as evidence about biology. Holding it fixed is both the better-scoring and the principled choice, so it cut all four of those arms to clear the queue, and the combination runs are now starting — stacking yesterday's two separate gains on one 77,760-parameter model to test whether they add. Anchoring suppresses precisely that.
